newsitem.title: UK: Siebe at record after Satchwell purchase.
newsitem.headline: Siebe at record after Satchwell purchase.

text.p: Shares in Siebe Plc nudged to a record high in a generally weak UK market on Thursday, after the acquisitive engineering group said it was buying Satchwell Controls Ltd from General Electric Co Plc.
The stock was up 6-1/2p at 10.88-1/2 stg by 1500 GMT, in modest volume of 727,873 shares, extending its surge from around 940p at the beginning of December.

Powered by strong underlying growth and well-received acquisitions, Siebe shares have doubled since the start of 1995. Last month it posted a 32 percent jump in pre-tax profits to 190 million stg, at the top of the range of analyst expectations.

Analysts said today's 80 million stg purchase of Satchwell from GEC was a promising addition to Siebe's controls businesses, though it was small beer for the company whose major acquisitions have included Unitech and Foxboro.
"For Siebe this is a relatively small acquisition," said one analyst, who asked not to be named.
"It is yet another infill acquisition, and the potential is evident from the fact that Siebe's controls business has an operating margin of 16 percent, while Satchwell has eight percent."

"It fits into the company's global network, Siebe's cash flow is giving it the ability to make these infill acquisitions and this is just an example of that trend, but it is not going to radically change perceptions of the stock," the analyst said.
Siebe was the tenth best performing stock in the FTSE 100 index through 1996. GEC shares were down 4-1/2p at 377-1/2, in line with a generally weaker UK market.
